prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1293; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported today by the insured driver, who says a vehicle merged into the lane during a lane change and scraped along the side of the insured car. The claimant's counsel has also sent a letter of representation, so all further contact will go through that office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted with the first notice. They show the damage on the passenger side and confirm some of the details in the driver's account, though they do not show the moment of contact.

Entry 3: Spoke with the insured, who confirmed the policy is in force and that the driver listed on the policy was operating the vehicle at the time. No earlier damage to the vehicle has been reported or found in the file.

Entry 4: Police report obtained. It places the claimant in the other vehicle and records the same location and approximate sequence of events the insured described. No independent witnesses were identified in the report or in any statement since.

Entry 5: Appraiser inspected the insured vehicle. The damage pattern matches the described impact, and the repair estimate reflects panels and components consistent with a sideswipe.

Entry 6: Received a medical summary from counsel listing neck and back strain as the injuries. The kind and force of the impact fit these complaints well, and no prior injury to the same body areas appears in the records supplied so far.

Entry 7: Claimant gave a recorded statement through counsel. The account matched the one given in the initial call, including the sequence of the lane change and the position of both vehicles.

Entry 8: Treatment records have arrived and show regular visits, with new services added over the following weeks. The volume of care is well above what is typically needed for a strain of this type, so the file is being flagged for medical review.

Entry 9: Spoke with counsel about the growing treatment list and asked for the referral notes and imaging that support the additional services. Counsel said the records would be sent but gave no timeline.

Entry 10: Reviewed the policy history. The coverage on the insured vehicle was active at the date of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage started.

Entry 11: Claimant's account has stayed consistent across every contact so far, including the call, the statement, and the medical intake. The file still rests on the photos, the police report, and the physical damage, with no independent witness to the contact itself.

Entry 12: Medical review requested. Pending its outcome, the injury portion remains open, the property damage is being prepared for payment, and counsel has been told the next update will follow once the outstanding records are received.
